mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, keep the signed subtraction order on both sides (e.g., (A − B) = (C − D)), never convert to absolute values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you encounter a sentence of the form “the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have”.
mathgap.example: Treating (A − B) = (C − D) as |A − B| = |C − D|, which loses sign information.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable’s numeric value becomes known, immediately substitute it into every pending equation and propagate any newly‑determined values further.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving any equation that yields a concrete number for a variable, replace that variable everywhere else before moving on.
mathgap.example: Finding Margaret = 16 but failing to replace Margaret with 16 in later equations, leaving those equations unsolvable.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, i.e., after all earlier statements (including transfers and direct counts) have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a sentence like “A has K more (fewer) tomatoes than B”, use the current values of A and B at that moment, not their final values after later statements.
mathgap.example: Using the final count of Lionel for a comparison that appears before Lionel’s later transfer, thereby ignoring the earlier state.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and ignore all unrelated constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before attempting to solve the whole system, trace from the query variable through every constraint to collect only the relevant subset.
mathgap.example: Trying to solve the entire 60‑variable system when the question only asks for Audra’s count, instead of extracting the sub‑graph that links Audra to the rest.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique capitalized token as a separate variable, even if two names differ by only a single character or look similar.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears, create a fresh variable unless the exact same token has been seen before.
mathgap.example: Merging “Leonard” and “Leona” into one variable, causing contradictory equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret phrases like “the difference between the number of X that A and B have” as the signed subtraction A − B, not as an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any “difference between … A and B …” construction.
mathgap.example: Reading “the difference between Helma and Gail” as |Helma − Gail| instead of Helma − Gail.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Translate “A has K more (fewer) items than B” into the signed equation A − B = K (or A − B = ‑K for “fewer”).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative phrase using “more” or “fewer” appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting “Ramon has 11 more tomatoes than Lyric” as Lyric − Ramon = 11, swapping the direction.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says “X has N items”, assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears in the narrative, treat it as an assignment that supersedes earlier information about X.
mathgap.example: Reading “Margaret has 16 tomatoes” as an additional constraint while still keeping a prior belief that Margaret = 15, instead of overriding it.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer (e.g., “X gives K items to Y”) immediately in the order it appears, subtracting K from the donor and adding K to the recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer sentence is encountered, update both parties’ counts right away before processing later statements.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, thereby using the wrong intermediate counts.

mathgap.title: Transfer as Equation for Unknown Counts
mathgap.principle: If a transfer involves a donor or recipient whose count is not yet known, represent the transfer as a linear equation linking the two variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When you see a transfer like “Eddy gives 12 tomatoes to Lyric” and either Eddy or Lyric is still unknown.
mathgap.example: Treating “Eddy gives 12 to Lyric” as Eddy = Lyric + 12, forgetting that Eddy also loses 12 (the correct relation is Eddy − Lyric = 24).

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the order of subtraction, treating “A has K more than B” as B − A = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map “A has K more than B” to the signed equation A − B = K (or A − B = ‑K for “fewer”).

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets “difference between A and B” as |A − B|, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the signed order when translating difference phrases; use A − B, not |A − B|.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers out of narrative order, mixing up intermediate counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfers strictly in the order they appear, updating counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct count is a permanent starting value, ignoring later overrides.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat each direct count as an assignment at that point, overwriting any previous value for that person.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies multiplicative changes before all other constraints are resolved, leading to inconsistent values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Only apply multiplicative statements when they explicitly appear, after the current count has been established.
